# Installation

You need FreeCAD with the OTTER add-on to set up a model, and at least one solver to run it.
The solvers do not need FreeCAD: the generated scripts are plain Python and can run on a
different machine, such as a compute server.

!!! note "Versions used for the benchmark"
    openEMS v0.37.0-rc1 with CSXCAD v0.7.0-rc1, **EMerge 3.0.0a6**, Palace 0.16.0 with
    OpenMPI 5.

## 1. The FreeCAD add-on

Install [FreeCAD](https://www.freecad.org/downloads.php) (1.0 or newer), then clone OTTER:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mohsen-alihosseini/OTTER
cd OTTER
```

Find your macro folder in FreeCAD under **Macro → Macros… → User macros location**
(on Linux usually `~/.local/share/FreeCAD/Macro`), then link the add-on into it:

=== "Linux / macOS"

    ```bash
    MACRO_DIR=~/.local/share/FreeCAD/Macro
    ln -s "$PWD/addon" "$MACRO_DIR/OTTER"
    cp addon/OTTER.FCMacro "$MACRO_DIR/OTTER.FCMacro"
    ```

=== "Windows"

    Copy (or `mklink /D`) the `addon` folder to
    `%APPDATA%\FreeCAD\Macro\OTTER`, and copy
    `addon\OTTER.FCMacro` to `%APPDATA%\FreeCAD\Macro\OTTER.FCMacro`.

Start it with **Macro → Macros… → OTTER.FCMacro → Execute**. The macro looks for the
add-on in a folder named `OTTER` next to it (or in its own folder), so keep that folder name.

OTTER is a standalone add-on. Its modules have their own names (`OtterDialog`, `utilsOtter`,
`OtterKiCADImporterToolDialog`, …), so it can be installed next to the original
FreeCAD-OpenEMS-Export (or an older copy of it) in the same macro folder; the two do not load
each other's code, even when both are opened in one FreeCAD session. Settings files (`.ini`)
of the original add-on can be loaded in OTTER.
Because the add-on is linked rather than copied, `git pull` in your OTTER clone updates it.

## 2. openEMS (FDTD)

Install openEMS and CSXCAD with their Python bindings by following the
[openEMS install guide](https://docs.openems.de/install.html). Then check:

```bash
python3 -c "import CSXCAD, openEMS; print('openEMS OK')"
```

The generated scripts also need `numpy` and `matplotlib`.
**AppCSXCAD** is optional; it shows the model and the mesh in 3D before you run.

## 3. EMerge (FEM)

```bash
python3 -m venv ~/venv_emerge
source ~/venv_emerge/bin/activate
pip install emerge==3.0.0a6  # pulls in gmsh, numpy, scipy, matplotlib (Python 3.10-3.13)
python3 -c "import emerge; print('EMerge OK')"
```

Install exactly this pre-release. The benchmark script uses `sim.set_scale_factor(1000)`,
which EMerge 2.8.5 does not have, and calls `sim.check_version("3.0.0")`, which stops on any
other major.minor version. Why the scaling is needed: [EMerge: version and scaling](user-guide/emerge.md#version-and-scaling).

Scripts generated by the add-on also import a helper package (STEP import, boundary
conditions, lumped ports), written by the author of FreeCAD-OpenEMS-Export. Install it into
the same environment:

```bash
pip install basicemergesolverhelperpackage==0.0.9
```

Without it the generated script stops at its first import with this install command.
Scripts with scale factor 1 (no micrometre parts) also run with EMerge 2.8.5.

## 4. Palace (FEM, MPI)

Palace is a compiled MPI program. The simplest install route is Spack:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/spack/spack.git ~/spack
. ~/spack/share/spack/setup-env.sh
spack install palace
spack load palace
which palace                 # the wrapper script
ls "$(dirname "$(which palace)")"/palace-*.bin   # the binary the run scripts use
```

The mesh is built in Python, so you also need `pip install gmsh numpy` (a virtual
environment is fine; pass its interpreter with `PY=…`). See the
[Palace install docs](https://awslabs.github.io/palace/stable/install/) for containers
and cluster builds.

!!! warning "Use the Palace binary under `mpirun`, not the `palace` wrapper"
    Under `mpirun`, the `palace` wrapper starts its own one-process run on every rank, and
    these runs crash on each other's output files (`json parse_error … empty input`). The
    OTTER run scripts (`run_palace.sh`, `run_all.sh`) therefore look for
    `palace-x86_64.bin` next to the wrapper. Set `PALACE_BIN=/path/to/palace-*.bin` if yours
    has another name.

## 5. Comparison scripts and documentation

```bash
pip install numpy matplotlib          # results/*.py
pip install mkdocs-material           # optional: build this website locally (mkdocs serve)
```
